title: Signal and Terminal
premise: Xanthe Villalobos, the last human technician aboard relay station Terminal Nine, intercepts a ship returning from deep space carrying a crew mysteriously aged backward — including a courier carrying an encrypted message that could end the decades-long war between Earth and the Outer Colonies. As factions race to seize or destroy the message, Xanthe discovers the reversal was no accident: the courier's faction weaponized time-dilation tech to smuggle truth past censors, and the message names the war's true architects on both sides. Hunted across the relay network by a corrupt fleet admiral and haunted by her own erased memories of the war's first crime, Xanthe must choose between broadcasting the message and preserving the fragile ceasefire it might shatter. In the end she splits the signal — sending proof of the architects' guilt to every world at once — forcing both governments to fall and a new, uneasy justice to begin outside any law.
about_author: Elodie Winterbourne is a former radio astronomer who left academia to write fiction about the silences between stars. She lives off-grid in coastal Norway, where she repairs lighthouse transmitters and insists the best science fiction is written by people who have watched a signal die.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Establishing her solitary routine maintaining Terminal Nine's dying relays along a route abandoned by war. She talks to automated ghosts and keeps a private log of worlds that stopped answering. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into purpose — someone must keep listening.

chapters.title: Return Vector
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A ship appears on a trajectory no living pilot could fly — the Meridian, lost eleven years ago. Docking clamps groan; inside, the crew are children wearing adult scars' worth of muscle memory. One, a girl with an old woman's eyes, presses a black cylinder into Xanthe's hands. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV as she examines the crew through medical diagnostics she barely understands. The reversal is real, uniform, and impossible — except the ship's logs show they experienced all eleven years. The girl-courier, Sef, speaks in fragments: 'They'll kill us before we finish growing.' Beat: horror and protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Message That Must Not Land
chapters.summary: Sef's fragmented POV, memories surfacing out of order. She reveals the cylinder holds testimony about the Kestrel Incident — the atrocity that started the war — naming admirals on both sides. Her faction aged the crew deliberately so border scanners would read them as children and wave them through. Beat: the weight of being a vessel for truth.

chapters.title: Admiral Voss Hails
chapters.summary: Antagonist intro, alternating Xanthe and intercepted fleet comms. Admiral Corvane Voss demands the Meridian be surrendered for 'quarantine.' Xanthe stalls, buying hours, realizing quarantine means incineration. Beat: the first open move in a game she didn't know she was playing.

chapters.title: Ghost Route
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She plots an escape through dead relays only she can reactivate, using her decade of maintenance knowledge as a map. Sef, physically six but mentally thirty, helps decode station locks. Beat: reluctant partnership forming; competence as intimacy.

chapters.title: What the Station Remembers
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. While rerouting power she finds archived traffic from the night of the Kestrel Incident — and her own authorization signature on a data purge she has no memory of performing. Someone edited her. Beat: self-doubt; the theme of memory turns inward.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter among the reversed crew, mostly Sef's POV. They remember careers, marriages, deaths; now they have decades ahead and nothing to show for them. Some want to surrender; some want to burn the message. Beat: grief for unlived lives, fracturing the group.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, humanizing him briefly — he too was at Kestrel, on the other side of the order. He burns a neutral relay to flush Xanthe out, killing three hundred sleepers in cryo. Beat: escalation; the cost of the hunt made concrete.

chapters.title: The Purge Signature
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She recovers a backup fragment proving her memories were wiped by a Colonial intelligence program she once served. She wasn't a bystander to the cover-up — she was its instrument. Beat: betrayal by her own past; rage with nowhere to aim it.

chapters.title: Terminal Eight
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Sef reach a half-dead station and find survivors of Voss's strike, led by a defected fleet medic, Okafor. They offer shelter and a transmitter array — if Xanthe shares the message. Beat: trust as currency; justice outside the law takes its first shape.

chapters.title: Two Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Interleaved POV: Colonial and Earth officials both learn the Meridian survived. Their private accord — jointly authored cover-up — is revealed to the reader though not yet to Xanthe. Beat: dramatic irony tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Sef's Decision
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The crew votes: broadcast everything, or trade the message for amnesty and new identities. Sef breaks the tie for broadcast, then confesses to Xanthe that the courier faction also falsified part of the record to guarantee Earth's guilt outweighed the Colonies'. Beat: idealism stained; truth needs editing, which makes it dangerous.

chapters.title: The Edited Truth
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Furious, she cross-references Sef's confession against her recovered purge fragment and finds the real sequence: both sides committed the atrocity, and her own hands sealed it. A clean broadcast would start the war anew. Beat: moral crisis at the story's hinge.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Lattice
chapters.summary: Action chapter, Xanthe's POV. Voss's strike team boards Terminal Eight during the transmission prep. Okafor dies holding the airlock; Xanthe escapes with the cylinder and two of the reversed crew through a coolant vent. Beat: loss, survival, guilt.

chapters.title: Voss Unmasked
chapters.summary: Alternating Voss and Xanthe POV. Cornered, Voss offers Xanthe a deal: her restored memories in exchange for the cylinder. He shows her the full Kestrel record — including the face of the intelligence officer who ordered her wipe. It is the face she now sees in mirrors, older. Beat: the enemy becomes a mirror.

chapters.title: The Third Signal
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, planning climax. She realizes neither government broadcast nor Voss's silence serves justice. She will split the message: raw evidence to independent colony networks, unedited, letting every world judge together — justice outside the law, distributed like light. Beat: resolve; the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, rapid-cut POVs. Xanthe chains every relay on the long route into one antenna while Sef holds Voss's boarding party at the docking ring with the ship's aging field — threatening to reverse him too. The signal goes out to forty worlds simultaneously. Beat: triumph paid for in blood.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Falling
chapters.summary: Multiple civilian POVs receiving the broadcast: protests, resignations, a fleet mutiny, Voss arrested by his own officers. Both governments wobble but hold — changed, diminished, forced into a joint tribunal they cannot control. Beat: justice arriving imperfectly, which is the only way it arrives.

chapters.title: Tribunal of the Reversed
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The reversed crew testify — adults in children's bodies, the only living witnesses. Xanthe testifies against herself, submitting her own purge signature as evidence. Beat: accountability turned inward; the theme of memory resolved into responsibility.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Offered a choice of experimental memory restoration, she accepts only partial return — enough to know what she did, not enough to be ruled by it. She and Sef, now aging forward again, repair Terminal Nine together. Beat: quiet reconciliation with the self.

chapters.title: Signal and Terminal
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Xanthe's POV, years later. New ships travel the long route; the relays carry honest traffic. Sef leaves for Earth to grow up properly. Xanthe stays, keeping the terminal lit, logging worlds that speak again. Final beat: the listener remains — because someone must keep listening.
